_about: BIP-37 M8.3 convergence target set, AS DATA. Every work-item state-write
site the census finds must appear here with a status and a reason. An
exclusion is a RECORDED DECISION, never an absence — a site missing from
this file fails the convergence test, which is how a new bypass announces
itself instead of arriving quietly.
v1's door governs the TRANSITION verb only: an existing work item's state
is reassigned. Birth-state (a row created carrying a state) is a different
verb the door does not accept yet, so those sites are excluded WITH that
reason rather than pretended away.
Every status below was set by READING the site, not by trusting the
scanner's verb or an earlier hand-written list. Four entries were
reclassified in the process, in both directions — see their reasons.
`lines` is SITE-GRANULAR and the guarantees read it: recorded sites and
census sites must be exactly equal. A new write inside an already-listed
file is therefore caught, which a file-set comparison missed. A CONVERGED
entry records no lines at all — it writes nothing, so it points at nothing.
THE CLAIM THIS FILE SUPPORTS IS BOUNDED, and the bound is the blind-spot
list below. Rowan demonstrated why that matters: a KNOWN instance of a
declared blind spot was live while the prose said all transition writers
had converged. A declared blind spot bounds a claim; it does not licence
leaving a known instance unscanned.

entries.reason: Intake acceptance moves an EXISTING issue out of TRIAGE to the project default. Existing row, state reassigned: exactly the verb the door governs. CONVERGED: `lines` is now empty because this site no longer writes state — a converged entry points at nothing, and that is enforced rather than trusted (previously it kept stale line numbers and nothing noticed; Vex, census review).

The app-surface twin of the api serializer above, same TRIAGE-to-default move on acceptance. Two surfaces, one rule — which is the drift the service exists to prevent. CONVERGED: `lines` is now empty because this site no longer writes state — a converged entry points at nothing, and that is enforced rather than trusted (previously it kept stale line numbers and nothing noticed; Vex, census review).

Auto-close reassigns the state of existing issues — the governed verb. CONVERGED under John's ruling of 2026-08-16, ATTRIBUTION FOLLOWS THE DECISION: an automated transition is attributed to the entity whose completed act triggered it, here the last entity that finished work on the issue before it went stale, because the close is a CONSEQUENCE of their act and of no one else's. An auto-deterministic function earns no credit; it reacted to a decision. This is honest where the previous attribution to project.created_by_id was not — that person in general never touched the issue. The operation records source=automation.auto_close so the ledger row can never be read as their manual click. EDGE, per the same ruling: if the triggering decider is no longer an active member with a write role at fire time, the transition is REFUSED and recorded rather than attributed to anyone else — their authority is what the close rested on and does not survive its loss (the BIP-67 precedent: absent a verified actor, write nothing). THE KNOWN BYPASS (Rowan 3860, EXECUTED on the dev board): IssueCreateSerializer exposes a writable state_id bound to `state`, and the app update route calls serializer.save() at app/views/issue/base.py:668-670. He drove the real serializer at the exact head — it accepted state_id, changed the stored state, and left BoardOperation.objects.count() == 0 while all 20 census tests passed. NOT YET CONVERGED: routing the primary issue-update path through the door is a real change to the main UI write path, and I will not rewrite it blind with no local test runner. Recorded as a live target rather than left invisible, which is the whole point of this file. The census now SEES this shape — a writable serializer field bound to state — so the declared serializer.save() blind spot no longer hides its known instance.

blind_spots: serializer.save() where the serializer sets state from validated_data — the state never appears at the call site
setattr(issue, 'state', ...) and any string-keyed attribute write
signals, and writes inside upstream Plane code this repository does not own
plain `import plane.board.service` is not walked by the convergence matcher — a real call through that idiom reads as unconverged (fail-safe; declared, not fixed)

the convergence matcher trusts the import binding, so post-import rebinding or local shadowing can false-positive — deliberately not fixed, scope tracking being real machinery against an implausible case
_blind_spot_note: A site reached ONLY through one of the shapes above will not appear in the
census and therefore cannot appear here. This list is the honest bound on
the claim: convergence proven by this file is convergence of what a static
scan can see, not of everything that exists.
